messages:
tara: kicking off q4f bring-up for cedar-v2 on canary (quant=Q4F-fast, kernel=packed-emb). Ran tri_locale_smoke (ja,ko,he). Weirdness: Korean outputs drop polite suffixes (요/니다) and Hebrew lines show embedded LTR comma before RTL closing quote. Anyone seen locale-sensitive detokenization regressions after quant packaging? :worried:

lucas: saw that too. quick numbers: ja->en BLEU -0.6, ko->en BLEU -2.4 (big), he->en BLEU -1.1. Repro command below:
```bash
python eval.py --model cedar-v2 --quant q4f --suite tri_locale_smoke --seed 7 --canary
```
Example (src ko): \uacf5\uc5f0\uc744 \uc9c0\uc6b0\ub294 \uacf3\uc5d0 \uc77c\ube44\uc0ac \ub0b4\uc5d0\uc11c \ud68c\ub2f9\uc744 \uc18c\uc2ec\ud558\ub294 \ub2e8\uc5b4\uc785\ub2c8\ub2e4.
Float32 output: 저는 그 방에서 회당을 소개합니다.
Q4F output: 저는 그 방에서 회당을 소개합니.
(note missing \uc694 /\ub2e4 polite ending token and punctuation shift)

mei: can you paste tokenizer id traces + tokenizer artifact version? if polite suffix token got merged into another id in packaging that would explain it. Also Korean uses compound morphs so subword splits matter.

lucas: tokenizer: cedar-spm v3.1 (artifact: cedar-spm-v3-2026-04-02.bin). Token ids (truncated):
Float32 ids: [120, 4550, 332, 98, 77, 4019, 11]  # 11 corresponds to polite-ending '니다' subtoken
Q4F ids:   [120, 4550, 332, 98, 77, 4801, 11]  # 4801 is an unrelated rare-piece, model seems to prefer different beam path

rashid: two angles: (A) packaging replaced spm binary with a rebuilt one (character_coverage tweak?) causing deterministic tokenization diff; (B) quant packing permuted embedding rows so the trained index->embedding mapping got mis-applied (embedding reorder). Try feeding float32 token ids into the q4f runtime (pretokenize feed) to see if ids->logits mapping preserves suffix.

lucas: did the pretokenize test. Feeding float ids into q4f model still drops suffix. So tokenizer is consistent but embedding lookup mapping differs. That points to a packaging reorder bug.

tara: packaging logs:
```
[2026-04-02T22:11:02Z] packaging: spm loaded (digest: sha256:bb77...c9ef)
[2026-04-02T22:11:12Z] quant_pack: embedding_pack v2 -> apply_permutation (perm.json)
[2026-04-02T22:11:12Z] quant_pack: detected sparse-to-dense remap for vocab subset
```
We did an embedding row re-order to compress sparse rows; maybe perm.json was generated against a different tokenizer ordering.

mei: aha. that explains it — reordering without a pinned vocab manifest can reassign rows. The polite suffix token is rare in train and may have been collapsed / moved. We should verify manifest-vocab.json vs spm vocab ordinals.

rashid: short-term mitigation: revert to embedding_pack v1 (no reordering) for canary and mark q4f packages as blocked until we audit perm generation. Long-term: add an assert that compares top-k token embeddings by checksum between float and quant bundles for a small token list (including locale-specific suffixes).

eval-bot: automated-eval: tri_locale_smoke | float32 BLEU(avg)=31.4 | q4f raw BLEU(avg)=29.2 | q4f pretokenized-ids BLEU(avg)=29.3 | notes: embeddings-permutation suspected (run=1748889000-audit)

lucas: thanks. I'll open an urgent PR to disable embedding reorder in quant pipeline and re-run onboarding. Also adding a locale-targeted token-checklist (ja honorifics, ko polite endings, he final forms) to onboarding checklist.

tara: rolling revert in canary now, will post results in ~10m. Also tagging infra to check perm.json generator provenance.

mei: can we add a small unit test in packaging that checks token->embedding mapping for ~50 locale-sensitive tokens using SHA1 of embedding row bytes? that would catch remaps early.

rashid: agreed. I'll add the test and a CI gate. Also propose we add a downstream smoke that validates morphological suffix preservation for agglutinative languages (ko, tr, fi) post-quant.

lucas: revert results: q4f BLEU(avg)=31.2 after disabling reorder, polite suffix preserved. Closing immediate block. Creating follow-up epic: ONBOARD-cedar-v2-embed-perm-audit.

tara: nice. please link the PRs. thanks all! :rocket:
